quest.title: Crisis at the Aisa Bathhouse
quest.description: You and Paimon follow the address on Mizuki's invitation and find your way to the Aisa Bathhouse. However, before you take the chance to enjoy a pleasant soak, it strikes you that business at the bathhouse isn't going so well...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x550, Mora x44000, Hero's Wit x5, Mystic Enhancement Ore x10

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aisa Bathhouse... Well, based on the letter, this should be the place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It looks familiar... Hm, we've walked past here several times before, right? Just never gone inside.

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: Are you here to visit the Aisa Bathhouse?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! Where'd you come from!?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: Oh, sorry... Forgive me, I didn't mean to intrude. We've been struggling to attract customers recently, so I got a little over-excited when I heard you discussing my bathhouse...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Your" bathhouse? So you run the place, huh? And business isn't going so great, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: Oops... please, forget I said that, it just slipped out. Now, do you have an appointment?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh... we have a VIP pass. Can we use it now?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: What? ...Ugh, I've told them before, a promotional gimmick isn't gonna magically fix our business. Who issued this thing... Wait, is that Miss Yumemizuki's signature?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry, I had no idea you were invited here by Miss Yumemizuki... Please, feel free to redeem your VIP pass now if you'd like. Just give your names at reception.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like she has a lot of clout... But aren't you supposed to be the boss?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: I am, yes, but Miss Yumemizuki is a major shareholder. The business never would've gotten off the ground without her investment...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What?

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: It's no cause for alarm though — she's a very responsible person. In addition to being a shareholder, she's also personally involved in our day-to-day business.

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: She only returned to Inazuma recently — otherwise, I'm sure you'd have heard of her by now. She's a highly renowned clinical psychologist.

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: Please, head on in.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: An indoor hot spring? Paimon's gotta give that a try!

dialogues.speaker: Flustered Attendant
dialogues.text: Hello! I'll be right with you— Aah!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, you okay?

dialogues.speaker: Flustered Attendant
dialogues.text: *grimace* ...Sorry! I'm so clumsy sometimes... But don't worry about me! Putting customers in a bad mood is the last thing I want.

dialogues.speaker: Flustered Attendant
dialogues.text: I promise I'll provide an excellent service! P—Please don't leave...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhh...

dialogues.speaker: Lazy Attendant
dialogues.text: How many times do I have to tell you? You breaking a few plates isn't the reason we've been losing business. Stop apologizing for yourself all the time — all it does is make you look like an easy target.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's all good, we're not out to target anyone... You didn't hurt yourself, did you?

dialogues.speaker: Flustered Attendant
dialogues.text: ...Nope, don't worry! As long as it didn't ruin your experience, that's all that matters! Now, um... looks like you'll be my first customers today, so, so... according to our standards of service, I need to, um, umm...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why is she so panicky...

dialogues.speaker: Lazy Attendant
dialogues.text: *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Actually, we're—

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Shion, let me see to these two. They're my guests.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aha, there she is! Baku lady is back!

dialogues.speaker: Shion
dialogues.text: So Mizuki invited you here? As VIPs? ...Does this mean you're gonna save the Bathhouse!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uhhh...

dialogues.speaker: Lazy Attendant
dialogues.text: She means, you must be very wealthy. Not everyone can afford our VIP service, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Lazy Attendant
dialogues.text: But a couple of customers with cash to splash doesn't solve anything in the long run. You should focus on what to do about our new competitor.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Aw, Murasaki, was that you showing some concern for our business? I'm touched.

dialogues.speaker: Murasaki
dialogues.text: Did not...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Since you're so eager to find solutions, you can work on our most pressing task — bringing our accounts up to date. With your smarts, I'm sure you'll fly through it.

dialogues.speaker: Murasaki
dialogues.text: ...Subtext being, you can't give it to Shion, because she's a moron and she'd screw it up?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Shion, I'll take things from here. What I'd like you to do is head to the kitchen and prepare some of your very best snacks for our VIPs.

dialogues.speaker: Shion
dialogues.text: Will do! That's my specialty...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Sorry to keep you waiting. I have to keep our staff calm to ensure you have the best experience.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: The panicky little girl is Hyakujitsuhaku Shion, and the lazy lady is Shiba Murasaki. They're both baku, just like me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait... so the older-looking one is actually younger? And the younger-looking one is older?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: That's right. How we choose to appear is just a matter of personal preference. It's more reflective of our personality than our age.

choices.text: Come on, Paimon. We've seen weirder stuff than this.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Anyway, enough about them — back to you two. Per the terms of the VIP pass, you're entitled to free use of all our services: so the spa, the fine dining, and psychological consultancy.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I would recommend starting with the psychological consultancy. Between me and you, one of the steps involves getting your bad dreams eaten.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #Since I ate one of {NICKNAME}'s good dreams by accident, this seemed like the best way to make amends.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, we get to have our bad dreams eaten by a yumekui-baku? That sounds fun!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: But is this a wise decision, given the current state of the business?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a good point. You've been having some difficulties recently, right? It wouldn't feel right to get all this free service while you're struggling... Is there anything we can do to help out?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...I take it you overheard Mr. Aikawa complaining about our current situation?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I am sorry to cause you concern. Mr. Aikawa is a smart businessman, but he tends to worry too much about short-term profits and lose sight of the big picture.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Our financial situation is nowhere near as dire as you're imagining. And in any case, passing our business woes onto our customers is hardly the solution.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Please enjoy the services we have to offer. Once you've experienced our hospitality for yourselves, I'm quite sure your confidence in our future prospects will be restored.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Can't argue with that! Let's get started!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Of course. The only thing is, psychological consultancy is a one-on-one service that takes quite a long time. But I can't just make one of you wait around while the other one is in therapy.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #So... Perhaps I can treat {NICKNAME} while Shion treats Paimon? Would that work?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fine by Paimon! But uh... is she up for it?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: She'll be fine. I noticed how gentle and encouraging you were towards her earlier. You're the perfect client for her.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, uh... hehe...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Secondly, Shion's therapeutic approach is a little different from mine... it often involves food. So she might be a better fit for you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Food therapy? Oh, that sounds perfect!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #Alright then, {NICKNAME}, please follow me.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Was all that just so you could be paired with me?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Don't get me wrong, Paimon is genuinely better suited to Shion. But in all honesty — yes, I had my own reasons for wanting to treat you myself.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Your psychology is so unique. I just had to investigate further to satisfy my own curiosity.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Please, come with me.

choices.text: Wow! I never would have guessed!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Before we begin, please take a seat on this chair.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: There's a theory which suggests that we bury our most powerful emotions deep within our dreams. That's the territory I would like to explore.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Before I start, I'm going to ask you a few questions. I want you to nod your head for yes and shake your head for no. Alright?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Very good. Now, I am going to plant a few thoughts in your subconscious, but it's nothing to get nervous about. Just a way to improve your sleep quality so the treatment will be more effective.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: What's the problem? Are you expecting me to bribe you with candy like a little child?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Are we going to keep testing my patience?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Are you... trying to relax your neck muscles? Remind me to teach you the proper technique some time.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #...{NICKNAME}? Hellooo? It's not time to fall asleep just yet.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: This is an incense from Sumeru that soothes the mind. The fragrance is said to be the "scent of dreams."

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Now, close your eyes, take a deep breath, and concentrate on the scent.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: The next step requires some visual preparation. So don't open your eyes until I say so.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Aw, where did it go?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: *sigh* I need to have a stern talk with Murasaki. How hard is it to just put things back where they came from...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Hmm... This needs another dab here.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Ahh, that's better.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What is Mizuki looking for? Surely it can't hurt to take a quick peek?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: I said no peeping... I'm still not ready yet.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Hey, don't run off now, darlings.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Come here.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: For goodness' sake, your butt's showing...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Alright, alright! Shh!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: "Darlings"? Now I'm curious... Maybe just a sneaky little peek?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: *sigh* Let me do that for you.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: I can see that you don't like being kept waiting. Go on, open your eyes. Everything's ready.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Ready. You can open your eyes now.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You kept your eyes closed the entire time! If only every patient was as compliant as you, it'd make our lives much easier... Here, you deserve a treat.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Take a good look at this painting — there are some very special little darlings hidden within it, and I'd like you to find them.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Do you see her? Isn't she just adorable?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Now, you just need to find the others.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh, are your eyes feeling sore? If so, please feel free to take a break.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Careful. When you look a psychologist directly in the eyes, they can see every little thing you are thinking.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: She's a baku as well. Whenever someone starts dozing off, she's there waiting for their dream to begin.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Your journey into dreamland began as you were looking for them. Feeling sleepy?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Now, I want you to take my hand.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: What's the matter? Feeling shy? Relax, this is just a part of the psychotherapeutic technique.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Very good. Now, close your eyes again for me.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: I want you to completely relax, and focus your attention on the feeling of my palm touching yours. Notice how all other sensations in your body are slowly fading away...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Now, imagine you're holding not my hand, but your favorite things in all of the world.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You run your hand through the sakura blossoms gently falling through the air, then through a squirrel's fur... Then you grab a fistful of sand on the beach...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You are once again in the wilderness, running with the wind at your back. But slowly, your palm loses sensation. You lose your way and find yourself surrounded by darkness.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You can't see anything. But you hear someone calling you... and now, a light is shining from the same direction as their voice...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (What is this place...?)

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, come over here...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Longing, caused by separation... It tastes so bitter. Please, don't stop moving.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Despair, caused by failure... Icy-cold on the lips. Please, keep going.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Regret, caused by missed opportunity... A sharp aftertaste. Please, don't look back.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Go to where the sakura petals fall, go to where the squirrels play, go to where you can hear the sound of the waves...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: That is where I am.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Holding my hand tight, those lost sensations come back to you...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: The feeling of running your hand through falling sakura blossoms, or through a squirrel's fur, or of grabbing a fistful of sand on the beach...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: And as you return from the wilderness, you gradually recover your other senses as well.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: We've reached the end of today's session. Don't get up yet, though — you were just in a very deep sleep, so you're probably still feeling a little groggy. I've switched to a different incense that'll help get rid of your drowsiness.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Yawn... How you getting along, {NICKNAME}?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Just finished.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: How are you feeling after your session, Paimon?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmm... Kinda... fresher and more relaxed? It feels... cozy, somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Good — that's exactly how you should feel after having a nightmare eaten. It sounds like the session was quite effective.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, for sure! Paimon especially liked how she used the sense of taste to help guide the process.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But Paimon was asleep for most of it, so she's not really sure how it all works. Do the yumekui-baku just, like... sneak into your brain and gulp down your bad dreams in one go?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: It's quite a bit more complicated than that. It deals with people's most visceral emotions, which have to be handled with the utmost care and attention...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounds super mysterious...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...Sorry, that probably made no sense at all. Anyway, don't worry about the details. For your purposes, Paimon, just think of it as Shion gulped your dreams away.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #How are you feeling, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: Just like Paimon described.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Really? Hmm... I still think there's more work to be done...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: You have quite a reputation for resilience and positivity. So, I expected to find very few negative emotions in you at all.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: But when I was deep in your subconscious earlier, the sheer weight of the emotions hidden there was overwhelming...

choices.text: Eh, I'm sure it's fine...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Well, even if you've buried those feelings deep enough to hide them from yourself, you can't hide them from a trained psychologist.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: But that's not what concerns me the most. Despite all your negative emotions, I couldn't find a single bad dream. So I just gave your mood a boost for now.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Huh. Well... maybe {F#s}he's just an eternal optimist at heart?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Optimist or not, everyone has bad dreams. Maybe they're just hidden even deeper in your mind... You're a unique case, as I suspected.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But {F#s}he said {F#s}he feels cozy, just like Paimon. So whatever you did, the treatment worked!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: True, but as a clinician, I would have hoped to reach a better understanding of my patient.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds like you want to keep researching me?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Fine by me, as long as you can put up with a daily nap while holding my hand.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Anyway, all jokes aside, it's time for you to try out the hot springs. Your mind has had the chance to de-stress, now it's time to do the same for your body.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ooh, that sounds good... Paimon's feeling relaxed already.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You know, this place provides a really great service. It's such a shame that you can't find more customers.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Don't start worrying about our bottom line again, or my work so far will count for nothing... Look — as long as we keep providing a great customer experience, we're sure to attract more business eventually.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm... If you say so.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #I think {NICKNAME}'s recovered from the therapy session now. Let's head to the hot springs.

choices.text: I... do have quite a lot of baggage from my past...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Yes. You certainly do.

choices.text: Cozy.

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Hmm... Most impressive, I must say...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Miko, what brings you here?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: Ah, there you are... I heard a rumor that you were about to be kidnapped. Naturally, I had to come and see it for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...She's joking, right? Paimon can never quite tell with her.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...Miko. It's been a while.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: You know each other?

dialogues.speaker: Yae Miko
dialogues.text: She never mentioned? Interesting... We've known each other since before I became the Guuji. I've told her all about you... but it sounds like she's forgotten all about me.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #You'll have to forgive me. I just didn't want to scare {NICKNAME} off... and "Hi, I'm Miko's friend" seemed like a sure-fire way to do that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Pff...

choices.text: Truth...

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Ah, I've missed your way with words.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: So, Lady Guuji. To what do we owe the honor?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Why, I simply came to see the business that my dear friend has invested in... Oh, and also to urge you to sell your shares before their value plummets to nothing.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: You could always invest in the Yae Publishing House, you know... Business is always booming. You only need to ask.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds serious... But what's wrong? Are the shares really gonna plummet to nothing?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Hasn't she told you? ...Tsk, of course. She's your therapist — she has the perfect excuse to never open up.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: The Aisa Bathhouse used to be very popular — although not because of the hot springs, despite the name. Their main selling point has always been the psychotherapy services offered by the baku.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: But recently, a competitor cropped up... His name is Emura Ichigensai. He operates right here on Narukami Island, and his methods are said to be quite revolutionary.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Since he provides a similar service to the bathhouse and boasts even better results, he was able to poach their entire clientele in just a matter of days.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh* It's such a pity to see how empty this place is now.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Miko, my job is to relieve my clients of their burdens — not to share mine with them.

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Of course you'd say that — you're a professional. But no amount of professionalism is going to fix this situation, is it?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: I heard people have been lining up since the early morning for Emura Ichigensai's clinic today — he's seeing patients just west of Inazuma City. And how many patients have you seen today?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Surely you know I'm not going to quit?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: *sigh* ...True, very true.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...So that's it? You're just gonna leave?

choices.text: Aren't you two friends?

response.speaker: Yae Miko
response.text: Oh, I'd love to help, little one. But I don't want to upset my old friend.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Miko's acting all mysterious again...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I understand why she doesn't want to help. The two of us are technically competitors, after all.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Light novels are one way for people to pursue happiness in their free time. So are hot springs, and so is therapy.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Miko and I disagree quite significantly over the question of how to make people happy.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is so confused by your friendship...

choices.text: It's definitely a quirky relationship.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon's curious though. After today, it's hard to believe that anyone could offer a better therapy service than the yumekui-baku. Which begs the question...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Who is this Emura Ichigensai guy, anyway?

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...Something of a mystery. I tried to look into his background when he first started poaching my customers, but I couldn't find anything.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: I suspect he's avoiding me on purpose, since I'm a competitor. In all this time, I haven't even figured out basic things like where he sees his patients.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, we at least know where he is today though, right? Miko happened to mention it in passing...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: That's true... But I'm sure he'll find a way to avoid me again if I go looking for him...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Then... why don't we go instead? We can pose as potential customers to get information out of him!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: As I keep reminding you, this is my problem, not yours...

choices.text: Unless the Aisa Bathhouse ends up having to close...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Exactly. You provide an amazing service here, and we want all our friends to experience it as well.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Huh. Well, now it just seems rude if I reject your help... In return, all I can offer is an even better service on your next visit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sure thing! Just leave this to us!

choices.text: ...In which case, it becomes our problem too.
It's definitely a complicated relationship.
Aren't you going to help?
I wouldn't go that far...

talks.objective: Go to the address Miko mentioned

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place... That guy looks official. Let's go ask him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hi there! We're looking for Emura Ichigensai, are we in the right—

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Pay first, take a ticket, then wait your turn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, okay...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ninety-seven... What number are you up to so far?

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Fifty-three. Be patient. I'll call your number when it's your turn.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Geez, what a charmer... Looks like we're in for a long wait, huh?

choices.text: Shall I knock him out, so we can barge straight in?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds kinda therapeutic in its own way... But we don't really have a good excuse to resort to violence here. And we definitely don't wanna scare off our target.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Why don't we pass the time by talking to some of his other patients? It looks like there's a few of them standing over there.

choices.text: Shall we talk to the other patients while we wait?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey, good idea! Hmm, it looks like there's a few of them over there. Let's go see what we can find out.

talks.objective: Ask around for information on Emura Ichigensai

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sorry to interrupt...

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Do I know you?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Show Ticket)

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: ...Ah, so you're here for counselling too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yep! Fellow clients of Emura Ichigensai here. Although, this'll be our first time using his service, so—

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: "Service"? How crass. We're talking about spiritual guidance here, not some business transaction!

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: In fairness to them, they haven't experienced it yet. Ignorance among the uninitiated is only to be expected.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Okay... Well anyway, Aisa Bathhouse calls it a service...

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Ah, more defectors from the bathhouse, huh? "Service" might have a veneer of professionalism, but all it really means is inadequate treatment that costs a fortune.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Why do you say that?

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: I'll tell you why. After just a few sessions with Emura Ichigensai, you'll completely forget about all your troubles. From then on, it's happy thoughts only!

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Today's supposed to be my last counselling session. He says that after we're done, nothing will ever trouble me again!

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Meanwhile, Aisa Bathhouse boasts about their strange and mysterious methods, but it's a total scam. They only treat the symptoms, not the root cause, meaning you have to go back time after time — all so they can keep charging you, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Exactly. Overpriced and ineffective. But counselling from Emura Ichigensai? I can't get enough! I know I'm done after today, but I'd take any excuse to keep coming back!

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: Me too... Probably see you tomorrow, then.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever the truth of the matter is, Paimon is starting to seriously dislike these guys!

choices.text: Stay calm, Paimon.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fine... Yeah, so we're mostly here to see what all the fuss is about. You guys seem to be experts by now — is there anything we need to do to prepare for our session?

response.speaker: Susukida
response.text: No, you don't need to do anything.

response.speaker: Susukida
response.text: Just show up, take a seat, and he takes care of the rest. I remember he lit some incense... it smelled wonderful, and instantly relaxed me...

response.speaker: Emura Ichigensai
response.text: I already know of the troubles that bring you to me.

response.speaker: Susukida
response.text: I don't know why I lose my temper so easily... I'm pretty messed up, right?

response.speaker: Emura Ichigensai
response.text: Yes, in the sense that all negative emotions are defects of the mind. But I can remove these defective feelings, leaving your mind healthy, whole, and free of distressing thoughts.

response.speaker: Emura Ichigensai
response.text: Now, receive my guidance...

response.speaker: Susukida
response.text: I don't actually remember the guidance... But anyway, it clearly worked. I guess whatever he said disappeared from my mind and took my problems along with it.

choices.text: Sounds a little unbelievable.

response.speaker: Susukida
response.text: So rude! Your counselling session will change your mind — in more ways than one!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We're only being cautious. What's wrong with that? You said it yourselves, the whole reason everyone's coming to this guy is because they're worried about getting scammed out of their Mora.

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: That's a fair point. You just need some reassurance, right? In that case... I can let you in on a little secret.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Go on...?

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: Well... someone in my family actually knew Emura Ichigensai before he made a name for himself. Apparently, he had a terrible temper. Pretty much everyone in the neighborhood had issues with him.

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: But he must've had some sort of epiphany, because he did a complete one-eighty. Went from having the most rotten temper you can imagine to one of the most cheerful people around.

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: Even more amazingly, all the people who used to despise him ended up becoming his best friends. His neighborhood's more peaceful and pleasant than it's ever been.

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: So you can rest assured that whatever treatment you get from Emura Ichigensai, he tried and tested it on himself first.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh... What a ridiculous story...

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: Doubt it all you want! I heard it straight from my relative, who knows him personally.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What should we do now? We may have burned our bridges with these two...

choices.text: At least we got some information.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! There's still a lot of people ahead of us, though... Why don't you take a rest while Paimon keeps watch? Just like how we do it out on the road.

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: The long wait makes you sleepy. Before you know it, you've fallen asleep...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You detect a faint fragrance, and begin following it to its source...

choices.text: Now to meet the man himself.
How can we be sure it works?
Remember, we're here to gather information.

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Pay first, take a ticket, then wait your turn.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Where am I?)
Let go of your pain...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (An eye!?)
...Who are you?
Argh... It burns...
Leave this place! NOW!!!
Let go of your pain...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, it's almost time!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (...Oh, it was just a dream.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yawn... that was a long wait. Paimon's gonna need a nap after this, too.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: No problem. It's my turn to keep watch anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alright! Now, time for us to go meet Mr. Emura Ichigensai!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh, hello! We're number 97. It should be our turn now, right?

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Uhhh... Yeah, sorry, the clinic's closed for the day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Why?

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Because Emura Ichigensai doesn't have limitless energy, that's why. He's gone home to rest. You'll have to try again tomorrow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But we've been waiting sooooo long!

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Not as long as some people. Try getting here earlier next time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Do you know where he lives, by any chance?

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Hah, save yourself the trouble. Spiritual masters like Emura Ichigensai cultivate their powers with peace and solitude. Someone like you ain't gonna find him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Drat. We shoulda barged in after all...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Let's report back to Mizuki for now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, nothing else we can do for today.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You tell Mizuki everything you saw and heard today.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: So he gives spiritual guidance... And it takes all your troubles away and leaves only happy thoughts?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yup. At least, that's what his clients say.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: How is that possible? Not even Mizuki could do that, and she's an incredible psychologist.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is that right? Paimon was gonna say, it all sounds too good to be true...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: It certainly is. Humans are... how to put this... they're a moody race — always upset about something. Show me a human without a care in the world, and I'll show you what "messed up" really looks like.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You think? 'Cause honestly, they sounded pretty convincing. And they said they only left the Aisa Bathhouse because they found it didn't deal with the root cause of their issues.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: But the idea he is spreading is categorically wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: That settles it, then. Emura Ichigensai is a quack, making false claims to steal all our customers.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Is that why he's doing this? To steal... steal our customers? Or is there more to it?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...It's unfortunate that you didn't get to meet him in person. I need some idea of the kind of person he is. Otherwise, I have no hope of figuring out his motivations and goals.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yeah, it's too bad... Although if it's any help, we did hear a bit about his backstory from someone else. Apparently, he used to have a really rotten temper, but then one day he suddenly reached enlightenment and became a spiritual master, or something...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Emura Ichigensai... rotten temper... Now wait just a minute...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Filing patient records is normally the most tedious job in the world. But once in a while, something mildly amusing grabs my attention. Take a look at this.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Emura Chuuya?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...It's him. I remember him.

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: Wait... That guy? Oh no...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What is it? What about him?

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Where to start? ...Imagine a big ball of negative emotion took on human form and started walking around. That's pretty much Emura Chuuya.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: His patient record mentions that he loved nothing more than a heated argument. No matter how trivial it was, he could never agree to disagree — he always had to be right. The happiest part of his day would be winning an argument and proving the other person wrong.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: If he lost, he'd sulk, and if anyone called him out, he'd throw a huge tantrum. Before long, he'd turned everyone against him.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sounds like he had issues...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Oh yeah. Serious issues.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Anyway, since no one would talk to him in real life anymore, he turned to the readers' letters column of a magazine by the Yae Publishing House, where he would attack writers and trade insults with other contributors.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Naturally, this ruined the column for everyone, and the editor soon started rejecting his letters.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Next thing you know, he's written a complaint letter to the Tenryou Commission, demanding that Inazuma pass a law to make it illegal for the Yae Publishing House to reject letters from readers...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Gee whizz... Where would you even start with a client like that?

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: In my case — by giving them a wide berth. Mizuki dealt with this guy.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: I'm pretty sure he only came here to try and start something. But Mizuki managed to get him into a session, and after some treatment, his mood improved by a lot.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wow. Great work, Mizuki!

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Murasaki makes him sound like a rabid animal... He wasn't THAT out of control. Sure, his personality was very abrasive, but it wasn't hard to see why.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Once I understood his situation, I was able to diagnose him very quickly...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You have very high expectations for yourself, but you've faced a lot of rejection in the past and haven't achieved much in your life.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You've never had any real close friends, so you don't know what healthy connections with other people look like. This puts you and your ego in the center of your world.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: In short, you long to feel a sense of accomplishment and to receive attention from other people. But both of these are lacking in your life.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: You have no idea how to properly deal with these emotions. So you've been taking it out on other people, partly to seek attention, and partly because you get a shallow sense of accomplishment whenever you win a war of words with another person.

dialogues.speaker: Emura Chuuya
dialogues.text: Tsk... You promise the world with your adverts, and that's seriously the best you can come up with? I'm not even going to bother explaining all the reasons you're wrong...

dialogues.speaker: Emura Chuuya
dialogues.text: I mean, you completely misunderstood why I even sent that complaint letter. The Yae Publishing House practically has a monopoly on Inazuma's publishing industry. How can they ignore what their readers have to say?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: In the magazine column you wrote to, your strongly worded letter appeared alongside dozens of others which praised the writer for their work. You can't talk about what their readers have to say without including them, too.

dialogues.speaker: Emura Chuuya
dialogues.text: No one with half a brain would praise a festering pile of garbage like that. Those are not opinions worth listening to.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: So, when I touched on the idea of you having an egocentric worldview — this is the kind of thing I was talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Emura Chuuya
dialogues.text: I... You...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow... How the heck did you get him to stay for treatment after dropping all of that on him?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Simple. The more he realized the truth of my diagnosis, the more he compulsively searched for evidence to refute it with.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: He'd lost the ability to communicate like a normal human being. So, I kept him here by using his preferred mode of interaction: argumentation.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: The Tenryou Commission had ignored his complaint letter, so he had no outlets left for his emotional outbursts.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Eventually, with the help of some incendiary words, I got him to agree to try some basic therapy. Finally, I was able to tweak his mood and stabilize his condition.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: It's a shame, really — if I'd only been able to see him a few more times, I know I could've helped him work through his personality issues. But unfortunately...

dialogues.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
dialogues.text: It was all my fault...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: For the last time, it was his fault for being a nutjob.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? What happened?

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Well, one day, he comes in as usual for therapy, but Mizuki isn't here. So, Shion sees him instead.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: I don't know what got into him that day, but he suddenly announced that he wished to be free of his troubles for good — and demanded that Shion make that happen.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Obviously, she didn't manage it, and then he pulled out a complaint letter to try and intimidate her. That was the last straw for me. I kicked him out and blacklisted him.

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: He hasn't shown his face here since.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Anyway, now everyone's had a look at his record — do we think there's any chance that this guy and Emura Ichigensai are the same person?

dialogues.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
dialogues.text: Because it sounds to me like after he didn't get what he wanted, he decided to have his revenge by lying to our customers and getting them to leave.

choices.text: That makes sense!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Bad dreams are formed from a buildup of negative emotions in the subconscious. You can't simply trick people into not having them anymore. If Murasaki was right, then surely they'd have seen his lies for what they are by now...

response.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
response.text: There's no point hemming and hawing! Let's report this guy to the Tenryou Commission for fraudulent business practices. If he can complain, so can we!

response.speaker: Susukida
response.text: Is anyone there?

response.speaker: Umihiko
response.text: We'd like to book a therapy session... Can we start now?

response.speaker: Hyakujitsuhaku Shion
response.text: Hello! Please come with me, I'll get you registered.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait, those are the two guys Paimon mentioned earlier! Just this morning, they were calling the bathhouse a scam and a rip-off. How are they back here already?

response.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
response.text: Oh really? Well, that proves it doesn't it? I was right. Now that they've realized they were lied to, they've come back.

response.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
response.text: So chin up, Mizuki. I bet you business will start picking up again from tomorrow morning.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! You yumekui-baku provide an unbeatable service, no scammer's gonna run you girls out of business!

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Interesting... Well, good. Murasaki, go help Shion please.

response.speaker: Shiba Murasaki
response.text: Tch... Shoulda kept my mouth shut. I jinxed it, and now I have to work again.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Now we just need to report this guy as a fraud to the Tenryou Commission, like Murasaki suggested. Problem solved!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It looks like the Aisa Bathhouse will be back in business in no time. No idea if our investigation actually helped, though...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Of course it did. You were a huge help, and I owe you big time for it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hehe...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Now then. You only got part way through the VIP experience last time, didn't you? You still have to try the hot springs and snacks. Both are top tier.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh, true! How could Paimon forget about that? Especially the snacks!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: After a dip in the hot springs and some delicious snacks, you and Paimon feel wonderfully relaxed.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow, Paimon feels incredible now. Nothing beats the complete service package!

choices.text: We should go talk to Mizuki about booking our next appointment.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Agreed! Although, Paimon didn't notice her inside just now. What could she be doing out at this hour? Hmm... Let's ask around.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey there, Mr. Aikawa. Do you have any idea where Mizuki went?

response.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
response.text: Oh, you're looking for Mizuki? She actually tends to disappear for a while around this time every evening. It's the one part of the day where she gets to relax herself.

response.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
response.text: As for where she goes and what she does during that time, I'm afraid I have no idea.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She takes the evenings to "relax," huh...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Like the first time we met her...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She probably tells people she's relaxing, but actually she's digesting the bad dreams, right? Hope she's not having any digestive trouble...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Remember the place from last time? Let's head there and check on her.

choices.text: Definitely coming back again.
Is it really that simple?

talks.objective: Go to where you first met Mizuki

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This should be the place...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: *crying*... *sigh*...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What? Why's Mizuki crying? Unless... Oh, maybe we got pulled into one of her bizarre dreams again?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}? Paimon? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Well firstly, we were hoping to get our next appointment booked in...

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: ...Ah, I see. I was planning on making it back before you finished in the hot springs, but I ended up spending longer here than I intended.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Don't worry, this isn't a dream. I was just... feeling a little sad.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aw, what's up? Indigestion getting you down again?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: No, my digestion was fine this time. What you saw just now was the aftermath of the digestion process.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Like I said, bad dreams are basically bundles of all kinds of negative emotions. When I digest them, I feel them all for myself.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: So when I'm processing these emotions, I tend to get quite... well, emotional.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Does that happen to all yumekui-baku?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Oh, don't worry about the others. To feel these emotions, you first have to understand them.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Most baku have a very poor understanding of humanity, so to them, a human bad dream just tastes like a slice of bland white bread. They can basically wolf it down and barely notice the flavor.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: I'm the odd one out in that sense. When I was studying abroad, I made a serious effort to learn as much about human psychology as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Now, I understand human emotions much better. I can empathize with them, and I can now discern many complex emotions when I turn my attention to digesting bad dreams.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: But still, that's no reason for you to be concerned about me. I wouldn't be much of a psychologist if I didn't have the mental fortitude to handle this stuff.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: Letting your emotions out is one of the most effective ways to process them. Now that I've done that, my mental state is back to normal.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thought maybe seeing those customers had upset you somehow.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It even makes Paimon mad! You work so hard for them, and then they turn around and accuse the bathhouse of being a money-making scam.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Yes, they were led astray by some swindler... but it's not like they took much persuading.

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: I can't blame them. The idea that you can forget all of your troubles and never have a bad dream again is a very alluring one. Who wouldn't want to believe that?

dialogues.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, if I really could make you forget all of your troubles for good, would you want me to try?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you imagine forgetting your pain and longing, the joy of reunion that you are looking forward to one day disappears along with it.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you imagine letting go of your hopelessness, you also feel your fighting spirit slip through your fingers.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: As you imagine being free from your painful regrets, the formative experiences of your journey lose their roots.

choices.text: But... if I forget all of that...

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: ...You really are different from other people.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Discovering what troubles people is easy for me — even in your case. But although I see your troubles clearly, I still don't completely understand you.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: *sigh*... Thanks for checking in on me. As a psychologist, I know how to take care of myself, but you showing that you care is still appreciated.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Anyway, it's much too late to book another appointment now... You should head home, get some sleep, have a wonderful dream, and come see me again tomorrow.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Alright. Goodnight!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Goodnight.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: Bye for now. If you still want to book another appointment tomorrow, make sure to come see me early.

response.speaker: Yumemizuki Mizuki
response.text: #{NICKNAME}, if I really could make you forget all of your troubles for good, would you want me to try?

choices.text: Would I even still be me?

dialogues.speaker: Kanai
dialogues.text: Uhhh... Yeah, sorry, the clinic's closed for the day.

dialogues.speaker: Aikawa Susumu
dialogues.text: Aren't you going to head inside? Believe me, Miss Yumemizuki will not disappoint!

dialogues.speaker: Susukida
dialogues.text: Do I know you?

dialogues.speaker: Umihiko
dialogues.text: ...What?
